Hi Alex / Sam,

Thanks again for the quick chat today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum on your competitive evaluation: 

- High-level takeaways from our call:
  - Acme is validating two vectors: 1) performance/cost for production traffic, and 2) operational reliability and incident response posture for customer-facing LLM features.
  - You want a direct comparator to hyperscaler endpoints (AWS Bedrock / Vertex) and a clear articulation of differences in incident response: escalation timelines, RCA cadence and detail, and rollback/fallback strategies.

- Proposed next tests:
  1) Short load window (2 days) with a 90th/99th latency capture to compare tail behavior across models/endpoints.
  2) Planned degradation simulation: we run a controlled error injection (5% increased error rate) during a 3-hour window to observe retries, fallback routing, and telemetry.
  3) SLA & RCA expectations doc: we will send a consolidated comparison (support ack times, P1/P2 handling, RCA delivery timelines, link to playbooks).

I've attached a draft RCA comparison table and a short SLA summary. Marissa / Neha, can you take the lead on the incident-response comparison and proposed test plan? Would like to share a one-pager with Acme by tomorrow EOD PST.

Alex, if that works, can you confirm the two contacts who should be on the test calls and whether you want us to route traffic from your US region only? Also share any guardrails you want for the degradation simulation.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

We're trying to understand the practical differences in communication cadence and the level of RCA detail (timeline, root cause, mitigation, long-term fix) across providers.

If you can include that in the one-pager (and explicitly note what Redwood commits to for P1/P2 and RCA timing), that would be super helpful.

Subject: Re: Fwd: ACME - incident response + SLA details, draft one-pager attached

Hi all,

Attached is a draft one-pager and an incident-test-plan. Summary highlights (TL;DR):

- Redwood commitments (Recommended standard):
  - P1: 15 minute ack (on-call), initial triage and status within 30-60 minutes, interim updates every 2-4 hours until remediation.
  - RCA for P1 incidents: preliminary RCA within 48 hours, final RCA within 5 business days with timeline, root cause, mitigation, and permanent fix plan.
  - P2: 4 hour ack, RCA within 5 business days.

- Practical differences vs hyperscalers (examples from recent customer engagements):
  - AWS (managed endpoints): often 1 hour P1 ack, interim status every 4 hours, RCA 48-72 hours. AWS provides deep infrastructure-level detail but may require an additional support contract for dedicated escalation.
  - GCP / Vertex: variable ack windows; RCAs can be longer (3-5 business days) depending on triage scope.
  - Anthropic / smaller API providers: faster hands-on engagement but may have limited automatic failover tooling; RCA depth varies.

- What we recommend for Acme testing:
  1) 2-day latency/load capture (baseline).
  2) 3-hour degradation sim in staging mirror (5-8% injected error rate) with Redwood routing fallback enabled (route to a lower-cost quantized model variant that has higher error tolerance).
  3) During the sim, Redwood will run on-call escalation: ack + first update within 30-60 mins; SLA metrics dashboard, traces and sampled transcripts will be shared within 8 hours.

Attachments in this draft: RCA-comparison-table.xlsx, SLA-summary.pdf, incident-test-plan.docx.

Neha, test-runbook looks good from my review; added a short checklist for telemetry hooks we should confirm with Acme (sampling rates, log retention). Vivek, I called out Dedicated vs Hosted differences in the appendix. Dedicated deployments can provide VPC-level failover and a private on-call escalation path if you need a named escalation contact.

Happy to iterate, giving you a short window to refine before I send to ACME today.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
